newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to miss criteria for EMU entry - Donges.
newsitem.headline: Germany to miss criteria for EMU entry - Donges.

text.p: Juergen Donges, one of the panel of the government's independent economic advisers known as the Five Wise Men, said on Friday Germany is likely to miss the criteria for entry to monetary union.
Donges told Reuters in an interview that he saw no real chance for Germany to meet the fiscal entry criteria, adding that this was the case both on the budget deficit and on the debt assessments.
He added that he did not believe that the stability pact on European monetary union provided full assurance that countries which took part in monetary union would maintain budgetary discipline.

Donges said that he believed that if monetary union, which is scheduled to begin in 1999, could not begin with a large enough group of countries then it would be better to delay the start. He added that it was more important to ensure that the criteria were met adequately than to start on time.
"History will measure monetary union on the criteria of whether it really produces a stable currency and not on the basis of whether it began on a certain day," he said.
Countries which wish to enter monetary union in 1999 must meet targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, total debt and public deficits this year.

For most countries, the deficit requirement, which calls for a deficit level of no more than three percent of domestic product, is proving the hardest to meet. Germany is aiming for a 2.9 percent level this year, which many see as over-optimistic.
On public debt, the ideal target is 60 percent of GDP. Countries with much higher debt levels must at least show that they are making progress toward that level.

Germany is currently running a debt level of just over 60 percent which is set to rise this year, but has already pleaded that the special situation of German unification should warrant it special treatment in the final assessment.
